$comment: Plutto's core and the signals people know it by. Sources: the plutto.space site source (/home/user/chedfox/plutto-web: app/page.js, app/about/page.js, app/layout.js, app/globals.css, app/components/*, app/icon.svg, public/floating-logo.png, tailwind.config.js, README.md) and the user's brief. Nothing here is invented; unknowns are listed under openQuestions.

core.belief: People have looked up for answers for thousands of years; the sky should be able to answer one person back, about their own chart, in plain words.
core.change: Instead of reading a sun-sign paragraph written for a twelfth of the world, you ask your own birth chart a question out loud and hear it explained, in the tradition you choose, by a voice that remembers you.
core.tension: The oldest way of asking (watching the sky) meets the newest way of answering (a voice you can interrupt). Thousands of years of looking up; now the sky talks back, to you, in conversation.
core.notThis: Not a horoscope, not twelve boxes, not fortune-telling. Plutto never claims to predict outcomes; it helps you explore patterns, time, choice and yourself.

pillars.name: Ask the sky
pillars.job: The customer's moment: the real kinds of questions people bring to astrology, written as example prompts with how Plutto would approach them. Never presented as testimonials.

pillars.name: Five lenses
pillars.job: Education: what each tradition is for (Vedic for exactness, Western for psychology, Chinese for the elements, KP, numerology for a name).

pillars.name: The craft
pillars.job: Proof: Swiss Ephemeris, 300+ classical yogas, 19 divisional charts, 7 dasha systems, 89 languages, voice on OpenAI Realtime.

pillars.name: Not twelve boxes
pillars.job: The dramatic truth: a sun sign is one of twelve; a birth chart is yours.

pillars.name: Coming soon
pillars.job: News (O6): Plutto for iOS and Android, soon. No date until the team gives one.

marks.$comment: Original files only. Never redraw, simplify, substitute or recolour them.

files.source: app/components/Nav.js (the site's header lockup), set as SVG with the site's own fonts via @import
files.what: "Plutto" in Cormorant Garamond 500 (28 px, tracking -0.025em, white) with "AN ASTROLOGY ORACLE" under it in Inter 400 (8 px, uppercase, tracking 0.4em, white at 45%), 2 px apart, line height 1. Baselines measured in Chromium from the site's markup.
The app icon: a gold (#D4AF37) ring and dot on a black rounded square (64 x 64, radius 14).
A real photo-like image: a dark planet with a thin blue rim on black space, a few stars. 1024 x 1024.

marks.usage: The wordmark lockup sits next to (or directly under) every headline (O4), scaled as one unit, always white on the dark ground; it is never re-set in the pairing's fonts. The app icon is used unchanged wherever an icon belongs: thumbnails, stories, banners and app-launch pieces. The icon and the orb are the only places gold appears.

colours.name: gold
colours.role: Only the orb and the app icon. The code calls the orb 'the single sacred place where gold lives'.

colours.name: white
colours.role: All type, at full strength or faded (white/45-75) for secondary lines.

type.role: Display serif (app/layout.js). Light for headlines, medium for the wordmark, italic for the turn ('speaks back.').
Body and the tiny spaced caps (0.32-0.42em) used for labels and the wordmark's line.

type.note: The site's README says Playfair Display, but layout.js loads Cormorant Garamond; the code wins.

signals.imagery: A black void with a few hand-placed stars (Starfield.js), a faint natal wheel (NatalWheel.js: 12 signs, 12 houses counted anticlockwise from the ascendant at 9 o'clock, a gold centre dot), and public/floating-logo.png: a dark planet edged with a thin blue rim.

signatureElements.what: The gold Oracle orb (Orb.js + globals.css): five radial-gradient layers (halo, body, specular, rim, shimmer), breathing 1.8% over 9 s.
signatureElements.rule: The orb is the brand's signature element and is drawn as the site draws it, with its own radial-gradient glow and stops. This is a brand element allowed despite Negative Space's no-gradient, no-glow default (art.json -> palette.rules), the same way the original marks are exempt from the palette. Its gold stays on the orb; no other gradient or glow appears in any piece.

signatureElements.what: A hairline chart wheel in white at low opacity, with the orb or a gold dot at its centre.
signatureElements.rule: Drawn precisely (12 signs, 12 houses, degree ticks, Noto Sans Symbols glyphs with text presentation) in Wada White hairlines; never decorative.
Used only for labels of one to three words (Negative Space typography.json allows caps labels at 0.08-0.14em; the brand's wider tracking is kept for brand labels).

signatureElements.what: Sparse hand-placed stars on the site background.
signatureElements.rule: Not drawn on flat pieces (Negative Space NS1: no decorative marks in the empty ground); real stars arrive with the floating-planet photo.

approach.why: Plutto already speaks in negative space: a black void, one gold object, 'quiet depth'. The style's evidence (white space reads as prestige, trust and quality: Pracejus, Olsen & O'Guinn 2006, 2013; less clutter raises attention to the brand: Pieters, Wedel & Batra 2010) fits an oracle that must feel exact and trustworthy, not mystical. Its palette rules allow dark grounds for night themes with text at 7:1; the night sky is literally the subject.

roles.accent: pyrite-yellow #cab356 (only where a flat gold is unavoidable; the orb itself keeps its brand stops)
roles.support: calamine-blue #78cdd0 (echoes the blue planet rim; not used flat in the launch)

palette.why: The only Wada combination holding Wada Black (closest to the void) and a gold (Pyrite Yellow, 33 RGB units from #D4AF37). Combination 149 has a closer gold (Olive Ocher) but its darkest colour is Deep Slate Green, a visibly green ground.

pairing.why: Instrument Serif is the closest pairing to Cormorant Garamond: a quiet, high-contrast, narrow display serif with a true italic for the brand's 'speaks back' turn; Instrument Sans plays Inter's neutral role; both rated core by Negative Space. bodoni-jost (Didone + geometric sans) is too fashion and Jost is unlike Inter; source is calmer but loses the display contrast.

guideChoices.glyphs: Astrological glyphs (zodiac signs, planets) are set in Noto Sans Symbols with U+FE0E so they never fall back to colour emoji. They are drawing symbols, not a typeface choice; flagged as an open question.
